executive_assessment.text: The CCDR estimates about 463 km2 of urban area is at high risk of flooding from rivers, rain and sea-level rise; many affected urban residents live in unplanned settlements without adequate drainage.
The CCDR says about 70 percent of Tanzania's population depends on agriculture, many as poor smallholder farmers, and is poorly positioned to manage repeated or simultaneous climate shocks.
The NDC sets a target to raise access to clean, safe water from 2015 baselines of 86 percent in urban areas and 67.7 percent in rural areas to 100 percent by 2030.

geographic_notes.text: northeastern Tanzania; southern Tanzania: The NDC reports average maximum temperatures rose over 1 degree C in 1961-2013 and drying occurred in northeastern and much of southern Tanzania during 1981-2016, affecting agriculture, water and energy.
